content.title: About
content.content: Light cream cheese is a soft cheese made from low‑fat curd, typically containing 5‑7 % fat. It has a mild, buttery flavor, a light texture, and is suitable for diet‑friendly meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: It is often used as a lower‑calorie substitute for regular cream cheese in recipes.
The light version retains most of the protein found in regular curd while significantly reducing fat.
In some countries it is classified as a separate dairy product rather than a cheese variety.
Manufacturers frequently fortify it with calcium and vitamin D to support bone health.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Light cream cheese provides about 10 g of protein per 100 g, helping maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: With fat levels usually under 7 %, it fits well into low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium contributes to strong bones and teeth and supports muscle function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Digestive ease
items.content: Lactose in light cream cheese is often lower than in regular dairy products, making it easier to digest for some people.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Shelf life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the product loses freshness quickly; keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Light cream cheese works well as a spread on bread, in smoothies, as a filling for rolls, casseroles, and desserts. Mix it with herbs, spices, or fruit for varied flavors.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. After opening, use within a week. Discard if it develops a sour smell or mold.
